bugs: Minor: a 2xx response that is not 201 is retried by throwing a RuntimeException (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:115), which risks a duplicate shipment if the partner returns 200 with an id. The Idempotency-Key header reduces this risk.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:129-145: the database claim/release logic for the notification is written as raw query-builder code inside the job, not as intent methods on the Order model.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:53: the condition `!== Sent && ! createShipment()` packs the control flow into one boolean expression, which makes it harder to read.
app/Models/Order.php:48: markAsPaid calls refresh() inside the transaction just to sync state, which costs an extra query.
strengths: failed() only marks the shipment failed while shipment_reference is null (whereNull guard), so a mail failure after shipping can never mark a shipped order as failed (confirmed by probe).
Permanent errors are surfaced without retrying: 422 fails the job with an InvalidShipmentAddress reason, and other 4xx responses such as 401 fail immediately.
The job refreshes the order at the start of handle() and checks trashed(), unpaid and already-failed before any HTTP call.

Modern queue attributes (Backoff, MaxExceptions, Timeout, DeleteWhenMissingModels), plus retryUntil, RateLimited with a global key, WithoutOverlapping, an Idempotency-Key header, and connect and request timeouts.
An atomic conditional update in markAsPaid, with the dispatch deferred by afterCommit.
The email is sent exactly once via the shipment_notified_at claim, which is released again if sending fails.
Good tests: 429 honouring Retry-After with a cap, 5xx, a hanging connection, 401, a missing id, the failed() guard, and an end-to-end run.

bugs: failed() calls markShipmentFailed with no guard (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:87-90). If the shipment was created but the mail keeps failing until MaxExceptions or retryUntil runs out, the order's status goes from sent to failed even though shipment_reference is set. Ops are misled and later runs skip the order (confirmed by probe).
Non-422 client errors (401, 403, 404, 400) are thrown and retried for up to an hour, up to 6 times, instead of being surfaced immediately (confirmed by probe: the job is not failed).
A missing or HTTP-date Retry-After header becomes 0, which is clamped to a 5s release. That is short for a partner that stays down for minutes, and each release also counts as an attempt.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:52-82: nested status conditionals check shipment_status three separate times.
app/Models/Order.php:36-40: uses ->value on enums in where()/update() even though the casts make this unnecessary.
app/Models/Order.php:33-56: the $claimed variable is shadowed inside and outside the closure, and the forceFill()->syncOriginal() after the transaction is extra ceremony.
app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:20: the retryUntil return type is Illuminate\Support\Carbon rather than DateTimeInterface.
app/Exceptions/ is an empty directory left behind.
strengths: Intent methods on the model (markShipmentSent, markShipmentFailed, claimShipmentNotification, releaseShipmentNotification) give a clean Eloquent API.
The failureReason() match expression produces readable, ops-friendly messages for 422, other HTTP failures, connection failures and anything else.
Uses #[WithoutRelations], DeleteWhenMissingModels, Backoff, MaxExceptions and Timeout attributes, plus RateLimited, WithoutOverlapping and an Idempotency-Key header.
The atomic conditional update in markAsPaid dispatches with afterCommit.
Thorough tests: one checks the rate limit is actually enforced, the configured URL is honoured, a real mail transport is used for the retry-once test, and a dataset covers failure reasons.

v.rationale: Both implementations use a very similar design: modern queue attributes, RateLimited plus WithoutOverlapping, an Idempotency-Key header, an atomic markAsPaid that dispatches after commit, and a claim column so the email is sent once. Both suites pass. The deciding difference came from the probes. impl-2's failed() handler marks the shipment failed with no guard, so an order that was shipped but whose email kept failing ends up with shipment_status failed even though shipment_reference is set. That misleads ops and breaks the requirement to show failed only when the shipment could not be created. impl-2 also retries permanent 4xx errors such as 401 for up to an hour. impl-1 guards failed() with whereNull('shipment_reference'), fails all non-429 4xx responses immediately, and refreshes the order before checking it. impl-2 has the nicer model API (intent methods) and a slightly richer test suite. impl-1's correctness on the focus area still outweighs that.
